producing an MSE of 18.38

title: ETTh1 improvement percentages (13.6 / 25.9 / 13.8 vs 15.7 / 33.8 / 18.6)

achieving the lowest MAE, MSE, and RMSE (13.6–25.9% better than Informer)
resolution: Decided: Table 4.2 stands. Over Informer: 15.7 / 33.8 / 18.6%. Over Autoformer: 11.5 / 15.9 / 8.3%. The thesis figures 13.6 / 25.9 / 13.8% are the gains over the mean of Informer and Autoformer. State the baseline or use the Informer figures; cite run three_models_comparison_ett_20260903_180948 (the run ending 165839 is the WTH run).

by grouping 16 time steps into a single patch with a stride of 4

resolution: Decided: no VRAM was measured. Remove the claim that it was recorded (or measure peak allocated memory and report it). The only VRAM figure to teach is the 6GB budget. Statements such as "least memory-intensive" are qualitative.

title: London Smart Meters: half-hourly and chronological, or daily and by household?
conflict: 3.2.4 and 4.1: half-hourly readings, over 3.4 million

resolution: Decided: describe it as daily, per-household records, split by household and concatenated for windowing; not aggregated across households. Correct 3.2.4, 3.3 and 4.1, state lookback and horizon in days, and add the window-crossing limitation.

title: One run per result, no seeds, no significance test

Author: one run per model per dataset; no seeds set (only the London household split uses seed 42)

resolution: Decided: add a caveat that every figure is a single run, so small gaps (Informer vs Autoformer on ETTh1) may lie within seed variance. Large margins (ETTh1 MSE 0.3742 vs 0.5652; Smart Meters 20.19 vs 38.67) are unlikely to be noise.
